Installation and quick start ​

WriteLikeMe is published on npm as @ai-clyde/writelikeme. It has no runtime dependencies, runs fully offline, and needs Node.js 14 or newer (18+ recommended).

Install ​

bash
npm install @ai-clyde/writelikeme
bash
pnpm add @ai-clyde/writelikeme
bash
yarn add @ai-clyde/writelikeme
bash
bun add @ai-clyde/writelikeme

Other ways to get it:

bash
npx -y @ai-clyde/writelikeme --help           # run once, no install
npm install -g @ai-clyde/writelikeme          # global `writelike-me` command
npm install --save-dev @ai-clyde/writelikeme  # pin it for a project's agents/scripts

Check that it works:

bash
npx writelike-me --version

Update with npm update @ai-clyde/writelikeme (or npm i -g @ai-clyde/writelikeme@latest). Remove with npm uninstall @ai-clyde/writelikeme.

Using an AI coding agent?

See AI harnesses for one-line MCP setup in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, VS Code, Windsurf and OpenCode, plus prompts to paste in.

Create your first SVG style code ​

From the command line:

bash
npx writelike-me generate -f my-writing.md -o style/me.svg
npx writelike-me brief --style-code style/me.svg

generate -o writes the SVG (creating folders as needed). brief prints a short, plain-language description of the style that you can paste into any AI chat.

From Node.js:

javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const WriteLikeMe = require('@ai-clyde/writelikeme');

const analysis = WriteLikeMe.analyzeText(fs.readFileSync('my-writing.md', 'utf8'));
fs.writeFileSync('writelikeme-code.svg', WriteLikeMe.generateStyleSVG(analysis));
console.log(WriteLikeMe.describeStyle(analysis));

Or in the browser: use the demo on the home page, which can also load an existing SVG and copy its style brief.

Command line ​

bash
writelike-me analyze  [text] [-f file] [--brief]
writelike-me generate [text] [-f file] [-o out.svg] [--width N] [--height N]
writelike-me brief    --style-code me.svg
writelike-me inspect  me.svg [--brief]
writelike-me write    --style-code me.svg "Write a short paragraph about community gardens."
writelike-me compare  "reference text" "candidate text"
writelike-me mcp
CommandWhat it does
analyzePrints style scores as JSON. --brief prints only categories, classification and the brief.
generateCreates the SVG. Without -o it prints the markup; without text it uses the neutral default profile.
briefPrints the style brief from an SVG (--style-code) or from text.
inspectPrints the profile stored in an SVG's metadata.
writeDeterministic, template-based draft. Not a language model.
compareHeuristic style similarity (0–1) and per-signal differences.
mcpStarts the MCP server for AI coding agents.

Text can come from positional words, -f/--file <path>, or stdin with - (cat post.md | writelike-me analyze - --brief). In a checkout of this repository, use npm run analyze -- "text", npm run generate -- -o me.svg "text", and so on.

Imports ​

javascript
// CommonJS
const WriteLikeMe = require('@ai-clyde/writelikeme');

// ES modules (Node.js imports the CommonJS default export)
import WriteLikeMe from '@ai-clyde/writelikeme';

// Agent Handler (also available as WriteLikeMe.Handler / WriteLikeMe.createHandler)
const { createHandler } = require('@ai-clyde/writelikeme/handler.js');

index.js is also a UMD script. In a plain web page, load it with <script src="https://unpkg.com/@ai-clyde/writelikeme/index.js"></script> and use window.WriteLikeMe. This is how the demo on this site runs.

Schema v3: what's inside the SVG ​

The SVG <metadata> carries a complete, versioned JSON profile:

  • Seven categories: formality, complexity, sentence_length, vocabulary, tone, creativity, punctuation
  • Voice cues: pronouns, contractions, sentence variation, paragraph length, question/exclamation rates, transitions, hedging
  • Habit signals: dialogue, all-caps, numbers, URLs, emoji, passive voice, punctuation rhythm, quote style
  • Grammar patterns: comma splices, semicolon use, run-on sentences
  • Sentence structure: simple / compound / complex rates
  • Readability: Flesch-Kincaid grade, reading ease, grade label
  • Style classification: formality level, dominant mood, voice, pacing
  • Domain: business / technical / academic / creative / legal / medical / general
  • Frequent words: up to five { word, count } entries

v1 and v2 style codes are upgraded to v3 automatically when read.

The SVG contains the profile and frequent words, not the original sample. Still, frequent words can reveal personal details, so inspect the file (writelike-me inspect me.svg) before sharing it.

Limitations ​

The analyzer uses dictionary and text-shape heuristics. It does not call an AI model or evaluate meaning, and results on short or non-English text are rough. Punctuation balance is not a grammar-correctness score. writeLikeMe() produces simple template drafts; for real writing, give the style brief to an AI model.
